Generate a provenance record for a catmech analysis

Source: R/audit-trail.R
catmech_audit_trail.Rd

Collects the R and package versions, SHA-256 hashes of the input data, the assumption specification and each completed dataset, the imputation settings, the convergence status and any pooled or sensitivity results into one document, in Markdown, JSON or standalone HTML.

Usage

catmech_audit_trail(
  object,
  pooled = NULL,
  sensitivity = NULL,
  format = c("markdown", "json", "html"),
  path = NULL,
  title = "Catmech Audit Trail & Provenance Report"
)

Arguments

object

A `catmech_result` object, or a list containing a `result` and optional downstream objects (`pooled`, `sensitivity`, `audit_plan`, `holdout_check`).

pooled

Optional pooled analysis object (`catmech_pooled_lm`, `catmech_pooled_glm`, or `catmech_pooled_coxph`).

sensitivity

Optional `catmech_sensitivity` object.

format

Output format: `"markdown"` (default), `"json"`, or `"html"`.

path

Optional file path to write the report to. If `NULL`, the character string is returned invisibly.

title

Document title (default: `"Catmech Audit Trail & Provenance Report"`).

Value

A character vector of class `c("catmech_audit_trail", "character")` containing the generated audit document.

Details

The input-data and completion hashes are taken by [digest::digest()] over the serialized R data frames, so they can be recomputed only in R, not with a file checksum tool. The specification hash is of its canonical JSON text, which [write_catmech()] saves as `assumptions.canonical.json`. The hashes let a rerun be compared with the record; they do not make the document tamper-evident, because anyone who edits the data can also regenerate the record. The record can support documentation, for example under FDA 21 CFR Part 11 or ICH E9, but compliance is a property of the validated system, access controls and procedures around it, not of this function.

Examples

set.seed(123)
df <- data.frame(
  lab = stats::rnorm(30, 10, 2),
  age = stats::rnorm(30, 50, 10),
  y = stats::rnorm(30, 5, 1)
)
df$ref <- df$lab
df$ref[11:30] <- NA
res <- catmech_reference(df, value = "lab", reference = "ref",
                         predictors = c("age", "y"), m = 2, seed = 1)
pooled <- catmech_pool_lm(res, y ~ lab + age)
trail <- catmech_audit_trail(res, pooled = pooled)
print(trail)
